title: Variable-field / magnetic centrifugal filter
alt: Two panels contrast an inward centrifugal end plug favoring light-ion escape with an outward magnetic mirror where rotation can favor heavier-ion escape.
mechanism: Rotation and magnetic-mirror barriers create different escape conditions at two ends.
pros: Two end conditions can direct light and heavy fractions to different outlets.
The separation coordinate is axial, which can simplify product access.
cons: Loss cones need collision-driven replenishment without excessive cross-field mixing.
Rotation, field geometry, end sheaths and collection must all be controlled.
limitations: Endpoint sketch only. A complete field, pitch-angle scattering, replenishment and throughput are not calculated.

title: Plasma-optical mass separation (POMS)
alt: Energetic ions enter a strong magnetic core region with thermionic electron emission; conceptual deflected paths reach separate collector zones.
mechanism: A strong magnetic core redirects energetic ions; electron emission and charge-separation fields participate in the optics.
pros: The tutorial reports separation experiments with nitrogen, argon and krypton.
Collection may occur at different radial or axial locations.
cons: The energetic source and nonuniform magnetic optics complicate the apparatus.
Electron emission and self-generated fields are needed for predictive optics.
limitations: Original conceptual layout. It is not a reconstruction of a POMS experiment or a calculated field/trajectory map.

title: Azimuthal-B / radial-E geometry
alt: An annular transverse cross-section shows an axial conductor, counterclockwise azimuthal B and outward radial E, with the ideal inverse-radius B and logarithmic potential equations.
mechanism: An axial central current creates Bθ∝1/r; a logarithmic radial potential alters ion orbits in an annular plasma.
pros: Calculations reviewed in the tutorial suggested separation with little ion deposition on electrodes.
cons: The cited concept requires a large central current and biased plasma electrodes.
Prescribed fields do not establish field penetration, sheaths or collection efficiency.
limitations: Ideal geometry and field laws only. This is distinct from POMS and from a magnetic cusp.

sources.title: Zweben, Gueroult & Fisch — Plasma mass separation (2018)
Author-hosted tutorial PDF (PPPL)

title: Radial advection
alt: A local E-right, B-out-of-page force diagram shows downward E-cross-B flow, upward neutral drag and the chain from rotation through friction to radial advection.
mechanism: Neutral friction on azimuthally rotating ions produces a cross-field radial drift; reduced mass and collision law affect species response.
pros: It may use rotation already present in a linear plasma.
It is relevant to understanding competing radial transport in other separators.
cons: The tutorial neutral-friction mass dependence is weak.
Spatial collision profiles, neutral composition and evolving density must be specified.
limitations: Local force-direction sketch. No neutral-rate calibration, evolved density profile or collection fraction is implied.

sources.title: Zweben, Gueroult & Fisch — Plasma mass separation (2018)
Author-hosted tutorial PDF (PPPL)

title: Radial diffusion
alt: Mass scaling equations show gyroradius squared growing with heavy mass while collision frequency falls inversely; two identical radial cumulative diffusion curves illustrate the resulting null separation.
mechanism: Randomized magnetized motion creates radial spread; in the tutorial heavy-on-light Coulomb limit the leading test-ion mass dependence cancels.
pros: Collisional, relatively cool and dense plasmas may reduce auxiliary heating needs.
cons: The tutorial classical Coulomb benchmark gives little or no heavy-mass separation.
Fluctuations and other collision channels can dominate the classical coefficient.
limitations: The overlaid curves intentionally coincide. Other collision operators require their own coefficients and applicability checks.

sources.title: Zweben, Gueroult & Fisch — Plasma mass separation (2018)
Author-hosted tutorial PDF (PPPL)

title: Ion mobility
alt: Two illustrative spreading ion profiles drift between bias electrodes; one has a faster mean at equal charge and collision frequency, beside the mobility equation.
mechanism: Electric forcing and collisional drag set a mean drift, while thermal diffusion broadens the species distribution.
pros: No applied magnetic field is required.
A collisional mass-dependent drift can provide a separation coordinate.
cons: Diffusion broadens the output and competes with the directed flow.
Debye shielding can prevent the assumed field from reaching a neutralized plasma.
Collision frequencies are species dependent, so equal ν is not a universal gas law.
limitations: Illustrative profiles assume equal positive charge and equal collision frequency; they are not calibrated output distributions.

sources.title: Zweben, Gueroult & Fisch — Plasma mass separation (2018)
Author-hosted tutorial PDF (PPPL)

title: Differential ionization energy
alt: A Maxwellian electron-energy curve crosses two hypothetical ionization thresholds; a process diagram separates an ionized product branch from neutral remainder.
mechanism: Electron energy control changes species-specific ionization; extraction must then separate ions from the remaining neutrals.
pros: Different ionization thresholds offer elemental or molecular selectivity.
Low-threshold species can be attractive targets.
cons: Broad electron distributions and gradual cross sections limit sharp selectivity.
Measured cross sections, recombination and extraction history are required for predictive fractions.
limitations: Hypothetical thresholds and a Maxwellian shape illustrate the mechanism; no measured atomic rates or product purities are plotted.

title: Transit time / moving collector
alt: A pulsed source sends equal-energy ions along a guide to a moving collector; exact ideal arrival markers for 40u and 250u at10eV over10m show time dispersion.
mechanism: A narrow pulsed energy packet disperses in time; synchronized moving collectors convert arrival-time differences into deposition positions.
pros: Arrival time is a direct separation coordinate.
Segmented collectors can make deposited fractions mechanically accessible.
cons: Energy spread, scattering and pulse width blur arrivals.
Slits and pulsed duty cycle reduce useful throughput.
A rapidly moving collector must operate in vacuum.
limitations: Arrival times are the exact ballistic fixed-energy limit; no source broadening, scattering, slit loss or collector efficiency is implied.

title: Rotating magnetic-field proposal
alt: Four colored magnetic vectors depict successive phases of a generic transverse rotating magnetic drive; a checklist identifies the missing induced electric field, plasma response and transport closures.
mechanism: The tutorial identifies separation using rotating magnetic fields as a distinct proposal and directs the reader to external references.
pros: [Inference] A time-dependent magnetic drive offers a different control mechanism from static electrode bias.
cons: Section II does not specify a complete quantitative field, plasma-response or collector model.
The induced electric field and current response must be included in any predictive implementation.
limitations: Generic rotating-field drive concept only. No separator geometry, mass selection, transport rate or performance is predicted.

sources.title: Zweben, Gueroult & Fisch — Plasma mass separation (2018)
Author-hosted tutorial PDF (PPPL)

title: Collisionality-gradient advection
alt: An illustrative increasing collision-frequency profile is linked to diamagnetic flow and a conditional species-dependent drift, with missing transport closures stated explicitly.
mechanism: A collisionality gradient combined with ion diamagnetic flow can produce a radial drift depending on species mass and energy.
pros: The tutorial cites a theoretical scheme with potentially substantial separation.
cons: The spatial gradients and applicable magnetized collision regime must be established.
Section II does not give a closed numerical transport model for this variant.
limitations: Illustrative collision-frequency gradient only. The direction, magnitude, collection and energetic cost of transport are not solved.

sources.title: Zweben, Gueroult & Fisch — Plasma mass separation (2018)
Author-hosted tutorial PDF (PPPL)

title: Capillary discharge / ion-wind separation
alt: A capillary between cathode and anode has a qualitative heavier-isotope enrichment region near the cathode; three competing explanations are listed without assigning a numerical enrichment.
mechanism: The tutorial reports heavier-isotope enrichment near a capillary cathode; differential ion–neutral friction was considered the most probable of several proposed explanations.
pros: The tutorial describes experimental isotope enrichment in neon and krypton discharges.
cons: The process appears slow and unlikely to provide high throughput.
Thermal diffusion, differential wall losses and ion–neutral friction must be distinguished rather than assumed to be one mechanism.
limitations: Qualitative report of enrichment and candidate mechanisms only. No isotope flux, discharge solution or enrichment factor is calculated.
